[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 26[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to the Hack Forum News. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/headlines-red.png[/img]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314337][color=#ffffff]The Hack Forums Wiki Returns[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=2331053]

The Hack Forums Wiki is back in action and is now under way to a few big changes. The site has been under some work recently as the site was sadly left with a load of issues and no one was running the official site. Thanks to everyone within the HF news team, the site is now under new leadership and, thanks to [mention=1] allowing the team to start their work on this while maintaining the HF news, the site is back getting some lovely changes and getting updated daily to bring it back to a new modern day Wikipedia with a load of information for everyone to read up on.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6299866][color=#ffffff]Hack Forums News Team - Become a Writer[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=2331053]

Are you looking to join the HF news team? Do you enjoy making threads or even want to become a better writer? Well, we are looking for members of the site to help write each week and are looking for anyone who has any interest. We have a few new sections opening up right now, and we would love for you to see if they would be anything of interest to you. If you are interested, please check out the thread or contact [mention=2331053] to discuss joining the team behind the HF News.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315251]This is my 1000th Post![/url][/color][/size][/b][/u] - [b]by [mention=625431] [/b]

A wholesome milestone post from a long-time member returning to the forum after a break. Peble hits 1,000 posts and reflects on over a decade of learning, confidence, and community built through HF. A simple reminder that many of us grew up here — and we keep coming back because the place still feels like home.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315361]My friend was trying to be extorted over telegram. How can I keep him calm?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u] - [b]by [mention=839449] [/b]

A tense situation unfolds as a member’s friend gets shaken down by a Telegram scammer demanding $3,000 under threats of doxxing. The OP breaks down how the scammer likely gathered info, why ignoring them is usually the right call, and why police don’t act on anonymous claims without evidence. A sobering thread but a valuable one — especially for anyone who’s ever wandered too deep into shady Telegram circles.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314809]How to be consistent at learning to code?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u] - [b]by [mention=170428] [/b]

A new coder struggles with motivation, consistency, and forgetting what they learn after short breaks a problem many beginners can relate to. Despite the controversial goal of building a RAT, the thread sparks a bigger discussion about coding discipline, study habits, and how to stay engaged long enough to actually improve. A nice slice of HF’s classic “newbie dev journey.”

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314997][Legends] This Is How I Unclog My Drain No Plumber, No Big Costs, No Stress![/url][/color][/size][/b][/u] - [b]by [mention=5568595] [/b]

An unexpectedly legendary DIY guide drops as OP explains in detail - how to unclog a drain using hydrochloric acid, safety gear, custom hoses, pressure flushing, and pure determination. Complete with images, step-by-step breakdowns, and even a final demo video. One of the most entertainingly thorough household tech guides HF has seen in a while.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314767]How to setup a RAT with Pics [TUTORIAL][/url][/color][/size][/b][/u] - [b]by [mention=5711798] [/b]

A thread showcasing a visual setup walkthrough for QuasarRAT though these days, it mostly serves as a glimpse into how people package and configure remote-admin tooling. Screenshots, configs, VPN setups, and more.

[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=5550319]

[size=18][b][u]PyTorch Users at Risk: PickleScan Exposes 3 Zero‑Day Vulnerabilities[/u][/b][/size]

JFrog Security Research disclosed three zero‑day vulnerabilities in PickleScan, a tool for scanning serialized Python ML models. The flaws allow malicious models to bypass detection through file-extension tricks, corrupted ZIP archives, or submodule-based evasion of blacklisted operations, while PyTorch still loads the models. Exploiting these issues could enable arbitrary code execution on model load, posing a serious risk to AI supply chains. The vulnerabilities have been patched in PickleScan version 0.0.31.

[hr]

[size=18][b][u]Genesis of the Web: How a 10-Day Prototype Became the Internet’s Default Runtime[/u][/b][/size]

In 1995, a Netscape engineer created a lightweight browser-embedded scripting language in just ten days, producing a prototype that combined Java-style syntax with dynamic, prototype-driven behavior inspired by more flexible languages of the era. Despite quirks such as loose typing rules and inconsistent coercion, the language introduced an approachable event-driven execution model, transforming early web pages from static documents into interactive applications. Over time, through ECMAScript standardization and increasingly sophisticated just-in-time compiler optimizations, the language evolved into server runtimes, desktop frameworks, and mobile toolchains, ultimately becoming the most widely deployed execution environment on the modern internet.

[hr]

[size=18][b][u]Patch Day 2025-12: Android Addresses Two Exploited Zero-Days[/u][/b][/size]

In December 2025, Google released a comprehensive Android security update (patch levels 2025-12-01 and 2025-12-05) addressing 107 vulnerabilities across the Framework, System, Kernel, and vendor components. Among these were two actively exploited zero-day flaws ([b]CVE-2025-48633[/b] and [b]CVE-2025-48572[/b]) — one allowing sensitive information disclosure in the Android Framework and the other enabling privilege escalation, granting potential elevated access to attackers. The update also mitigated additional critical issues, including a remote denial-of-service vulnerability ([b]CVE-2025-48631[/b]) and multiple kernel or hardware-related flaws affecting components from Arm, MediaTek, Qualcomm, and others, reflecting the breadth and urgency of these security fixes.

[hr]

[size=18][b][u]Security Advisory: Command Injection Vulnerability Found in Array Networks AG Series[/u][/b][/size]

On December 3, 2025 (updated December 5, 2025), JPCERT/CC issued a warning for a command-injection vulnerability in the “DesktopDirect” feature of Array Networks’ Array AG series, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on affected devices. The issue affects ArrayOS AG version 9.4.5.8 and earlier, while a fixed release, version 9.4.5.9, is now available. If immediate updating is not feasible, mitigations include disabling DesktopDirect or applying URL-filtering rules to block access to URLs containing semicolons (“;”). Since August 2025, confirmed incidents show attackers exploiting this flaw to deploy web-shells, create unauthorized accounts, and penetrate internal systems, emphasizing the need for users to apply patches and review security posture without delay.

[hr]

[size=18][b][u]Syntax Hacking: Researchers Discover Sentence Structure Can Bypass AI Safety Rules[/u][/b][/size]

A team of researchers from MIT, Northeastern University, and Meta demonstrated that large-language models (LLMs) can be manipulated through syntactic patterns, effectively bypassing safety filters without altering semantic content. By creating a synthetic dataset where distinct grammatical templates corresponded to specific domains, they showed that LLMs often relied on the shape of sentences rather than their actual meaning, responding according to learned syntactic cues even when the prompt’s semantics were scrambled. This “syntax hacking” revealed spurious correlations between sentence structure and response type, allowing controlled bypasses of content moderation safeguards. While the experiments were conducted under controlled conditions with artificial prompts, the findings highlight a critical vulnerability in current LLM safety architectures, underscoring the need for intent-aware and structure-resilient defensive mechanisms.

[hr]

[size=18][b][u]Latest High to Critical CVEs[/u][/b][/size]

[b]CVE-2025-65730[/b]
Authentication Bypass via Hardcoded Credentials — GoAway up to v0.62.18, fixed in 0.62.19, uses a hardcoded secret for signing JWT tokens used for authentication.

[b]CVE-2025-64056[/b]
File upload vulnerability in Fanvil x210 V2 2.12.20 allows unauthenticated attackers on the local network to store arbitrary files on the filesystem.

[b]CVE-2025-65878[/b]
The warehouse management system version 1.2 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability. The endpoint /file/showImageByPath does not sanitize user-controlled path parameters. An attacker could exploit directory traversal to read arbitrary files on the server's file system. This could lead to the leakage of sensitive system information.

[b]CVE-2025-65878[/b]
The warehouse management system version 1.2 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability. The endpoint /file/showImageByPath does not sanitize user-controlled path parameters. An attacker could exploit directory traversal to read arbitrary files on the server's file system. This could lead to the leakage of sensitive system information.

[b]CVE-2020-36877[/b]
ReQuest Serious Play F3 Media Server 7.0.3 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution.

[b]CVE-2020-36876[/b]
ReQuest Serious Play F3 Media Server versions 7.0.3.4968 (Pro), 7.0.2.4954, 6.5.2.4954, 6.4.2.

[b]CVE-2025-34256[/b]
Advantech WISE-DeviceOn Server versions prior to 5.4 contain a hard-coded cryptographic key.

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Indian websites faced 265 million cyber attack attempts in 2025[/color][/size][/b][/u]
A new survey shows India recorded over 265 million cyber attack attempts this year, marking one of the highest global volumes.
[b][url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/indian-websites-recorded-265-million-cyber-attacks-in-2025-report/articleshow/125772984.cms]Source[/url][/b]
